title: About one man in twelve has a color-vision deficiency
summary: The National Eye Institute says about 1 in 12 men have color vision deficiency, and that men are at much higher risk than women.
body: A 'did you know' note on the National Eye Institute color-blindness page says about 1 in 12 men have color vision deficiency. The risk section says men have a much higher risk than women, and that the deficiency usually runs in families. Most people who have it are born with it. The page was updated on 5 November 2025. The fraction is the institute's figure, not a local clinic count.

sources.title: Color Blindness

sources.note: Supports about 1 in 12 men, a higher risk in men than in women, and the usual inherited pattern.
